business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 1 Business)
business_model.claim: Bentley Systems develops and markets infrastructure engineering software spanning modeling, simulation, enterprise cloud collaboration, asset analytics, and digital twin platforms across the project and asset lifecycle.
quotes: Bentley Systems is the infrastructure engineering software company.
We serve enterprises and professionals across the infrastructure lifecycle, from the design and construction of new projects to the operation and maintenance of existing assets.
Bentley Open Applications and Seequent applications are primarily cloud-connected desktop modeling and simulation applications that support the breadth of engineering and geoprofessional disciplines.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item (10-K Item 7 MD&A)
business_model.claim: Bentley Systems generates revenues from subscriptions, perpetual licenses, and services, with subscriptions representing 92% and total recurring revenues representing 93% of total revenues in the year ended December 31, 2025.
quotes: We generate revenues from subscriptions, perpetual licenses, and services.
We believe that subscription revenues will continue to comprise a majority of our total revenues.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-Q Consolidated Statements of Operations and Item 2 MD&A)
business_model.claim: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total revenues were $1,256,415 (table in thousands), comprising subscriptions of $1,157,938, perpetual licenses of 31,395, and services of 67,082 (all figures in thousands).
quotes: All amounts presented in this Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, except share and per share amounts, are presented in thousands.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 7 MD&A and Q3 2026 8-K Exhibit 99.1)
business_model.claim: Annualized recurring revenues were $1,582.8 million as of September 30, 2026, while recurring contracts with consumption measurement durations under one year accounted for 51% of total ARR (including 46% from E365) as of December 31, 2025.
quotes: Annualized Recurring Revenues (“ARR”) were $1,582.8 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $1,405.2 million as of September 30, 2025.

ARR resulting from the annualization of recurring contracts with consumption measurement durations of less than one year, as a percentage of total ARR, was 51%, 50%, and 47% as of December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively, with our E365 subscription offering representing 46%, 45%, and 41% of total ARR as of December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-Q Item 2 MD&A and Q3 2026 8-K Exhibit 99.1)
business_model.claim: In October 2026, Bentley Systems divested its non-software Cohesive consulting business—accounting for approximately 3.5% of year-to-date total revenues and approximately 50% of services revenues—into Naviam, and acquired seismic interpretation software company Eliis.
quotes: On October 13, 2026, we completed the divestiture of Cohesive—a business that provides IBM Maximo‑related implementation and consulting services and operated separately from our infrastructure engineering software offerings—by contributing it to Naviam, a leading IBM Maximo partner.
On a year‑to‑date basis, Cohesive represented approximately 3.5% of our total revenues and approximately 50% of our services revenues.
On October 29, 2026, we completed the acquisition of Eliis, a seismic interpretation software company.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1 Business and Q3 2026 8-K Exhibit 99.1)
business_model.claim: Bentley Systems serves engineering firms and owner-operators across Public Works/Utilities (approximately 59% of sector-attributable ARR), Resources (approximately 27%), Industrial (approximately 9%), and Commercial/Facilities (approximately 5%).
quotes: Founded in 1984 by engineers for engineers, Bentley is the partner of choice for engineering firms and owner-operators worldwide, with software that spans engineering disciplines, industry sectors, and all phases of the infrastructure lifecycle.

•Public Works/Utilities, which represents approximately 59% of our sector-attributable annualized recurring revenues (“ARR”)(1)(2), includes roads, rail, bridges, tunnels, airports, and ports; federal, state, and municipal agencies; and networks for electricity, gas, water, wastewater, and communications;

•Resources, which represents approximately 27% of our sector-attributable ARR(1)(2), includes mining, oil and gas upstream activities, offshore, pipelines, environmental management, and renewable energy;
•Industrial, which represents approximately 9% of our sector-attributable ARR(1)(2), includes process and discrete manufacturing, oil and gas downstream activities, and power generation; and
•Commercial/Facilities, which represents approximately 5% of our sector-attributable ARR(1)(2), includes campuses, office buildings, retail facilities, and hospitals.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Item 7 MD&A)
business_model.claim: The company sells in 189 countries and in 2025 generated 59% of total revenues outside the U.S., 94% from direct sales channels, 6% from indirect channel partners, and no more than 2% from its largest account.
quotes: We sell our software in 189 countries, primarily through a direct sales force located throughout the world.
Approximately 59%, 58%, and 58% of our total revenues were from outside the U.S. for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
Sales through our global network of independent regional channel partners accounted for 6%, 7%, and 8% of our total revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 7 MD&A and 10-Q Item 2 MD&A)
business_model.claim: Bentley Systems manages its global business within a single reportable segment dedicated to the development and marketing of computer software and related services.
quotes: We manage our business globally within one reportable segment, the development and marketing of computer software and related services, which is consistent with how our chief operating decision maker (“CODM”) reviews and manages our business.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 7 MD&A and 10-Q Item 2 MD&A)
business_model.claim: Organic revenue growth is driven primarily by expanding subscriptions within existing accounts—reflected in a 110% last twelve-months recurring revenues dollar-based net retention rate as of September 30, 2026—alongside 3% growth from new accounts in the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: The majority of our revenue growth, excluding the impact from acquisitions, is driven by additional subscriptions revenues from existing accounts using the same products.
Last twelve-months recurring revenues dollar-based net retention rate(2) was 110% as of September 30, 2026, compared to 109% as of September 30, 2025;

For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, subscriptions revenues increased $42,526 ($44,066 on a constant currency basis) and $137,875 ($129,182 on a constant currency basis), respectively, primarily driven by expansion from accounts with revenues in the same period in the prior year (“existing accounts”), and growth of 3% attributable to new accounts, most notably small- and medium-sized accounts.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors, 10-K Item 7 MD&A, and 10-Q Item 2 MD&A)
business_model.claim: Reported revenues are also moved by foreign currency exchange rates (with 33% of 2025 total revenues denominated outside the U.S. dollar), infrastructure spending cycles, China market challenges, and the October 13, 2026 Cohesive divestiture.
quotes: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, 33%, 34%, and 35%, respectively, of our total revenues were denominated in a currency other than the U.S. dollar.

The future results in China remain uncertain as a result of continued geopolitical challenges, the obstacles there to cloud‑deployed software, and the financial timing impact of the preference there for license sales, rather than subscriptions.

Because our prior period results include Cohesive and our results following October 13, 2026 will not, we expect year‑over‑year services revenues and cost of services expenses to decline through 2027, with a favorable impact on gross margin.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 7 MD&A and 10-Q Item 2 MD&A)
business_model.claim: Variable headcount-related costs represented approximately 80% of aggregate cost of revenues, R&D, selling and marketing, and G&A expenses in 2023 through 2025, and drove 2026 operating expense increases through compensation, bonuses, stock-based compensation, and corporate headcount expansion.
quotes: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, approximately 80% of our aggregate cost of revenues, research and development, selling and marketing, and general and administrative expenses were represented by what we refer to herein as “headcount‑related” costs.
Our headcount‑related costs are variable in nature.
We actively manage these costs to align to our trending run rate of revenue performance, with the objective of enhancing visibility and predictability of resulting operating profit margins.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items (10-K Item 7 MD&A and 10-Q Item 2 MD&A)
business_model.claim: Additional cost drivers include cloud-related costs (up $12,196 on a constant currency basis in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, MD&A in thousands), capitalized ACDP and intangible amortization, promotional spending, and currency movements on the 45% of 2025 operating expenses denominated outside the U.S. dollar.
quotes: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, on a constant currency basis, cost of subscriptions and licenses expenses increased primarily due to an increase in cloud-related costs of $12,196, partially offset by lower amortization of capitalized costs under our ACDP of $4,090.

For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, approximately 33%, 34%, and 35%, respectively, of our total revenues and 45%, 42%, and 45%, respectively, of our total operating expenses were denominated in a currency other than the U.S. dollar including most significantly: euros, British pounds, Canadian dollars, Australian dollars, Chinese yuan renminbi, and New Zealand dollars.
Other than the natural hedge attributable to matching revenues and expenses in the same currencies, we do not currently hedge foreign currency exposure.

This comprehensiveness provides diversification for our own business, as an incidental advantage.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business)

We take care to enable compatibility across successive generations of our applications, which enables engineers, throughout their careers, to maintain continuity with their preferred interfaces, formats, and methodologies, while advancing their work at the leading edge of innovation.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Customer consolidation, acquisitions, or management changes threaten Bentley's competitive position if acquiring firms or new leaders standardize on rival software.
quotes: If an existing account is acquired by another company that uses the software of one of our competitors, we may lose business in that account to our competitor.

Any such consolidation, acquisition, or management change could lead to pricing pressure, erosion of our margins, loss of accounts, and loss of market share, all of which could harm our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Customers have no contractual obligation to renew subscriptions, exposing Bentley to churn or slower growth from competing offerings, pricing, or budget cuts.
quotes: Our accounts are not obligated to renew their subscriptions for our offerings, and they may elect not to renew.

Account renewal rates may decline or fluctuate due to a number of factors, including offering pricing, competitive offerings, account satisfaction, and reductions in account spending levels or account activity due to economic downturns or financial markets uncertainty.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Bentley faces execution risk in cross-selling additional and acquired software offerings if customers view them as unnecessary or unattractive.
quotes: A significant component of our growth strategy is to increase the cross‑selling of our software offerings to current and future accounts, however, we may not be successful in doing so if our accounts find our additional offerings to be unnecessary or unattractive.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Bentley's AI and data-centric strategy faces threats from slow user adoption, flawed implementation or marketing, rising R&D costs, and expanding AI regulations and potential litigation.
quotes: As with many innovations, there may be slow adoption, regulatory challenges, or we may fail to appropriately implement and market our data-centric and AI-powered offerings.

Against this regulatory backdrop, our offerings based on AI may expose us to additional lawsuits and regulatory investigations and subject us to legal liability as well as brand and reputational harm.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Limited intellectual property protection leaves Bentley exposed to competitors developing or patenting similar or superior offerings or challenging and designing around its IP.
quotes: The steps we take may not be adequate to protect our technologies and intellectual property, our patent and trademark applications may not lead to issued patents or registered trademarks, others may develop or patent similar or superior technologies or offerings, and our patents, trademarks, and other intellectual property may be challenged, invalidated, designed around, or circumvented by others.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Software defects, interoperability failures with third-party products, and cybersecurity breaches on Bentley's or third-party cloud systems threaten customer trust, retention, and liability.
quotes: Further, the combined use of our software with those of other software providers may cause errors or failures, or it may expose undetected defects, errors, or failures in our software.

Any security breach could result in a loss of confidence in the security of our products and services, damage our reputation, negatively impact our future sales, disrupt our business, and lead to regulatory inquiry and legal liability.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Cyclical downturns across infrastructure sectors and potential cuts in government infrastructure spending could reduce software demand and contract renewals while sticky personnel costs constrain expense adjustments.
quotes: If participants in any of these sectors reduce spending or allocate future funding in a manner that results in fewer infrastructure improvement or expansion projects, then our accounts’ underlying business may be impacted and demand for our software may decrease or our rate of contract renewals may decrease.
Additionally, government spending on infrastructure may decrease, which could decrease the demand for our software and have a negative impact on our results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: With 33%, 34%, and 35% of total revenues over the last three full fiscal years denominated in non-U.S. currencies, Bentley's unhedged revenue and profitability are vulnerable to U.S. dollar appreciation as well as foreign regulatory, tariff, and privacy laws.
quotes: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, 33%, 34%, and 35%, respectively, of our total revenues were denominated in a currency other than the U.S. dollar.
Our revenues and results of operations are adversely affected when the U.S. dollar strengthens relative to other currencies and are positively affected when the U.S. dollar weakens.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A) and P3 (10-K Item 7)
competitive_position.claim: APAC including China accounts for 18% of total revenues, where Chinese operations face ongoing geopolitical challenges, obstacles to cloud-deployed software, and customer preference for perpetual licenses over subscriptions.
quotes: Approximately 18% of our total revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023 relate to infrastructure projects in APAC, including China.

The future results in China remain uncertain as a result of continued geopolitical challenges, the obstacles there to cloud‑deployed software, and the financial timing impact of the preference there for license sales, rather than subscriptions.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A Risk Factors)
competitive_position.claim: Acquisition-led growth carries risks of technology integration difficulties, failure to realize synergies, loss of key personnel or accounts, and entering markets where rivals hold stronger positions.
quotes: Even if we are able to consummate acquisitions that we believe will be successful, these transactions present many risks including, among others, failing to achieve anticipated synergies and revenue increases, difficulty incorporating and integrating the acquired technologies or software solutions with our offerings and existing applications, difficulties managing an acquired company’s technologies or lines of business or entering new markets where we have limited prior experience or where competitors may have stronger market positions, the loss of key colleagues, accounts, and channel partners of ours or of the acquired company, and the requirement to test and assimilate the internal control processes of the acquired business in accordance with the requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2022.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Item 1A) and P3 supplemental revenue table (10-K Item 7)
competitive_position.claim: Reliance on indirect channel partners for 6%, 7%, and 8% of total revenues over the last three full fiscal years reduces direct end-user visibility and creates partner termination and compliance risks.
quotes: Sales through our global network of independent regional channel partners accounted for 6%, 7%, and 8% of our total revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.

Where we rely on channel partners, we may have reduced contact with ultimate users that purchase through such channel partners, thereby making it more difficult to establish brand awareness, ensure proper installation, service ongoing requirements, estimate demand, and respond to the evolving needs of an account.
